neighbours.label: the inverted verb after 'nor' in a negated addition (', nor is it...', ', nor does it...'): adding a further negative claim, the other side of the + pole's 'also'; not plain negation and not affirmative 'and also'
fire: The room was not large, nor was it especially quiet at night.
The answer is not obvious, nor is it written in the manual.
The bridge is not wide, nor is it strong enough for lorries.
His story was not true, nor was it very convincing to the jury.
The soup was not hot, nor was it seasoned with any salt.
The path is not marked on the map, nor is it lit after dark.
The deal is not fair, nor does it help the smaller farmers.
The film was not long, nor was it boring for the children.
quiet: The room was large, and it was also quiet at night.
The answer is obvious, and it is also written in the manual.
The bridge is wide, and it is also strong enough for lorries.
His story was true, and it was also very convincing to the jury.
The soup was hot, and it was also seasoned with plenty of salt.
The path is marked on the map, and it is also lit after dark.
The deal is fair, and it also helps the smaller farmers.
The film was long, and the children enjoyed every minute of it.
